solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Smells surround a minor operation to pump organs

indicators.note: the smell word is split open to go around the rest

parts.note: to hum is informal British for to smell bad, so smells gives hums

indicators.note: an operation works on the words a minor, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Unpleasant odours hang around a small surgical procedure for pumping a patient's organs.
explanation.walkthrough: To hum is British slang for to smell bad. 'pump organs' is not medical: these are reed organs whose bellows are worked by pumping pedals.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonium is a small keyboard instrument whose reeds are sounded by air from foot-pumped bellows.

indicators.note: returns tells us the instrument word comes back the other way

parts.note: a tuba is a large brass instrument

explanation.surface: Someone next door hands back an instrument they borrowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour something, as a verb, is to lie next to it, which is what abutting means.

clue.text: Bond, say, turned on soft light

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after what it sits on

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light

indicators.note: turned means the example abbreviation is flipped round

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A bond, for instance, was switched on by a soft lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a binding promise or a security given, both senses of bond.

definitions.meaning: an academic subject: the science of matter and energy
an old word for medicines, especially purgatives, given by a physician

explanation.definitionFit: Physics is a school and university discipline, and in older English physics were medicines or remedies.

clue.text: Solvers will even like sound of Christmas

indicators.note: like sound of says the phrase is spoken to give the entry

parts.note: solvers are you, so solvers will is you'll; even means level, tied

explanation.surface: Crossword solvers will even enjoy the noise of the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken together, YOU'LL ('Solvers will') and TIED ('even', as in level) make the festive word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is the old name for the Christmas season.

clue.text: Organised Labour in true can-do fashion without Conservative leader

indicators.note: fashion, as a verb, means shape anew, rearranging the letters
without says a letter is taken out of can-do
the leader of Conservative is its first letter

explanation.surface: The labour movement is acting in a genuinely positive, can-do way, now without a Tory at the helm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes C ('Conservative leader') from CAN-DO to leave ANDO; 'fashion' then rearranges IN + TRUE + ANDO.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade union is an organised association of workers, so it is labour organised.

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight has been given attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to receive money in return for work, that is to be paid.

clue.text: Group in Kuala Lumpur with a hot esoteric doctrine

indicators.note: in puts the band's name inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: Abba is the Swedish pop group
H is the abbreviation for hot, on taps

explanation.surface: A band in the Malaysian capital is keen on a hot mystical teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Kabbalah is the Jewish mystical tradition, a body of secret teaching open only to initiates.

indicators.note: gone off, like a gun firing or food spoiling, signals the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter, so the fodder is just the six letters of airgun

explanation.surface: A Siberian's air rifle has fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugrian names peoples and languages of western Siberia, such as the Khanty and Mansi.

indicators.note: largely means only most of the name is used, its opening letters dropped

parts.note: Gromit is the dog in the Wallace and Gromit animations

explanation.surface: Wallace's companion was mostly edited from the film.
explanation.walkthrough: GROMIT is the beagle in Nick Park's British claymation films; four of his six letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit is to leave out, a synonym of cut out.

parts.note: a family tree is kept up to record people born into the line, so one of its aims is a new offspring entry

explanation.surface: A gardener states one goal of looking after a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree is a family tree, not one in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A family tree exists to trace offspring, each person in a later generation of the line.

parts.note: the surfer is on the internet, not the waves, and being connected means having a network link

explanation.surface: A wave rider with good contacts has a certain standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone browsing the web with a working connection is said to be connected to the internet.

indicators.note: folds means the letters are bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: A rash appears in the dirtier creases of the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the anagram fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Intertrigo is an inflammation of the skin where two surfaces rub together, a kind of rash.

clue.text: Tending to set short clue about intelligence, is hard to follow

indicators.note: hard to follow says the hard letter comes after the rest
about means the trimmed word goes around the intelligence measure
short means the word clue loses its final letter

parts.note: IQ is the intelligence quotient
H is the pencil marking for hard

explanation.surface: A setter's brief hint about intelligence is difficult to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is a social group, not a crossword setter; 'Tending to set' means inclined to form a clique.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliquish describes people inclined to form exclusive social groups, a set being such a group.

clue.text: Buffoon fell with force and cry of pain

parts.note: Scafell is a Lake District fell, and its opening SCA stands for it here, a loose but blog-confirmed reading
to ram is to force something in
ouch is what someone cries when hurt

explanation.surface: A clown fell over hard and yelled out in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: A fell is a hill in northern England; Scafell is the second-highest English mountain, and the setter takes SCA from it. 'with' and 'and' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaramouch is the boastful, cowardly clown of Italian commedia dell'arte, a stock buffoon.

clue.text: Cheek of young male holding race for second

indicators.note: holding means the young male word is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: a buck is a young man, or the male of deer and rabbits
the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

indicators.note: second means the second letter of the word for is taken

explanation.surface: A lad has the nerve to keep a race going for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheek' is a buttock, not impudence; 'for second' looks like time but picks the O of 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek is an informal word for each of the two rounded halves of the backside.

clue.text: He'll sit uncomfortably on rough ocean

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after the piece it sits upon
a rough ocean is churned up, so its letters are scrambled
sitting uncomfortably means shifting, so the letters of sit are moved

explanation.surface: He will be sitting awkwardly on a stormy sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He'll' is the whole definition: a person who will sit on the water. Both 'uncomfortably' and 'rough' are anagram signals, one per word, and 'on' stacks the second piece below the first in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe paddler is a person who will sit, often uncomfortably, on rough water.

clue.text: Roll of dice in roll-back and taxi

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled dice inside the reversed roll
back means the bread word is read in reverse

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

indicators.note: a roll of dice tumbles them, so the letters of dice are rearranged

explanation.surface: A throw of the dice takes place in a rollback, plus a taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal signal 'back' sits inside the hyphenated 'roll-back'. A bap is a British soft bread roll, and its reversal is PAB, which wraps the shuffled dice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicab is a pedal-powered rickshaw used as a taxi.

clue.text: Condition of leaving will challenge a country's borders

parts.note: a test is a challenge

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: A will may challenge the borders of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Testacy is the legal state of having died with a valid will in place.

indicators.note: mess, as in making a mess of, means the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter, so the fodder is the eight letters of sergeant

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out in the sergeants' mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the military dining room but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to alienate them from each other, ending their closeness.

parts.note: the dwarf is a miniature tree, trained in a Japanese art of pruning and wiring

explanation.surface: Someone in the East is coaching a very short person.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees in pots by careful pruning.

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A narcotic plant comes from Durban.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a large tropical herbaceous plant as well as its fruit.

annotationWithheld.why: Watch final - loser can't dance (CHARLESTON): H (Watch final) + LOSER CANT rearranged gives the answer, but the only anagram signal is 'dance', which is also the definition

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is found inside the words lethal force

explanation.surface: Someone should apply deadly force in proportion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' tells the solver to use the words that follow as the hidden word's text.
explanation.definitionFit: A half is a fraction or portion of a whole, so a proportion.

clue.text: Barbarian begins bowing out of rugby

indicators.note: begins means the beginning of each word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: A Barbarians player starts by bowing out of rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbarians are a famous British invitational rugby union team, so the surface reads like a player retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: A boor is a crude, ill-mannered person, a figurative barbarian.

indicators.note: reported says the word is spoken, giving an entry that sounds alike

parts.note: wound, as in wound into a ball, gives balled

explanation.surface: An injury left uncovered is reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past of wind: yarn wound up is balled.
explanation.definitionFit: A bald head or bald tyre is bare, uncovered and so exposed.

indicators.note: bewildered means confused, so the letters of signal are mixed up

explanation.surface: A signal confuses friendly nations.
explanation.definitionFit: To align oneself with someone is to ally with them, taking their side.

indicators.note: in puts the French police officer inside the abbreviation

parts.note: flic is French slang for a police officer

explanation.surface: A French policeman is caught up in a long-running clash.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflict is a fight or serious disagreement, a clash.
